newsitem.title: PERU: MOBIL DE PERU SEES 1997 GASOLINE SALES DOUBLING.
newsitem.headline: MOBIL DE PERU SEES 1997 GASOLINE SALES DOUBLING.

text.p: Mobil Corp's Peruvian susidiary, Mobil Oil de Peru, expects its gasoline sales to double this year to $400 million, company officials said Tuesday.
The increase in sales is due to Mobil de Peru's "aggressive marketing strategy", spokeswoman Cynthia Piedra said in a brief interview, without giving details.
Mobil, which has more than a 20 percent share of the gasoline market in Peru, budgeted to invest about $10 million in the sector this year, according to company officials.
Mobil competes in the gasoline market with Anglo-Dutch oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell, Texaco Inc of the U.S, Argentina's and Spain's Repsol SA.
Mobil also owns a lubricants unit, has a stake in a refinery and operates exploration projects in Peru.
